title: Unbounded RPC can block failover and orderly worker shutdown
original_condition: In the original baseline, an established remote RPC call could wait indefinitely, including while a chain-selection mutex was held, preventing failover and orderly shutdown.

SubmitMembership and SubmitILNGovernance select a verified URL, then create txrelayer.NewTxRelayer without injecting the bounded client or worker shutdown context. Both run preflight reads through relayer.Client and then SendTransaction. The node-owned txrelayer creates its own legacy jsonrpc.NewClient. The pinned ethgo HTTP transport constructs a fasthttp client without read/write deadlines and calls Do; those defaults are unlimited. Its Close method has no cancellation effect. WithReceiptTimeout changes the sleep between receipt polls, not the timeout of GetTransactionReceipt or any other HTTP call. Separately, chain-selection locks still span bounded provider I/O, finality polling can continue to five minutes after cancellation, and native receipt polling has a two-minute outer deadline without the worker shutdown context. Unbounded external submission/preflight I/O can still hold a worker and orderly shutdown despite read-side cancellation. Per-call or polling-loop limits on other clients do not impose deadlines on this separate transport. No live consensus stall is asserted. Actual consensus halt was not demonstrated.
